children.name: Description
children.characters: Linux is an open-source operating system kernel that powers a wide range of devices, from personal computers and servers to smartphones and supercomputers.

children.name: Description
children.characters: Linux was originally created by Linus Torvalds in 1991. Today, it has become one of the most important foundations of modern computing.

children.name: Description
children.characters: The core is only the beginning.

children.name: Description
children.characters: The kernel connects software to hardware. A complete distribution adds system tools, applications, and a package manager.

children.name: Description
children.characters: The source is public. Study, modify, and distribute it under the applicable licenses.

children.name: Description
children.characters: Many distributions are available without licensing fees. Shape your desktop, tools, and workflow.

children.name: Description
children.characters: User permissions, access controls, and security mechanisms help protect systems. No system is invulnerable.
